speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are here for chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To understand your condition better, have you noticed any blood in your urine, pain during urination, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing those details. Since your symptoms have persisted for five months and haven't improved with NSAIDs, have you experienced any lower abdominal pain that worsens when your bladder is full, or any difficulty starting your urine stream? Also, have you noticed any vaginal discharge or unusual odor?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

The history of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, frequency without infection, and dyspareunia is classic for this condition, especially given the lack of response to NSAIDs and absence of pyuria symptoms.
